name: CA-18
label: Safe D

key_factors: Longtime incumbent Zoe Lofgren running for re-election
Huge fundraising gap: Lofgren $1.7M raised vs. under $61K for Lewis
Prediction markets price Lofgren near certain to win
model.rationale: The district's D+16 lean, Lofgren's incumbency, and her roughly 28-to-1 fundraising advantage over Shane Lewis all point to an easy Democratic hold, and Polymarket prices her win probability at 97%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, this stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Lofgren or unexpectedly low turnout in a low-profile general could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Zoe Lofgren, a long-serving Democratic incumbent, is heavily favored to win re-election in this San Jose-area district that leans Democratic by 16 points. She advanced to the general election and has raised about $1.7 million, with $643,000 on hand and modest outside support, while Republican Shane Lewis has raised only about $60,000 with minimal cash remaining.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Lofgren roughly a 97% chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial edge makes this one of the safest Democratic holds on the 2026 House map.
